# Decision log
Every choice between alternatives, and every gap the code or sources leave that we filled ourselves. IDs are permanent. To change a decision, add a new entry and set the old one's status to "superseded by" the new ID; do not rewrite it. If the new entry replaces only part of it, keep the status accepted and add "partly superseded by D<n>: <which part>" (`check` reads that as partial and warns about no citations of it).

## D1. Build the layer around the optimiser, not another GA engine (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The 2024 Genetic Optimization Engine (GOE) was proposed for revival to tune simple_complex_v1's
  TwinProp training knobs: 100-200 evaluations, each a 4-10 min Slurm GPU job, noisy (SE about 0.03, as large as the
  differences sought). A survey of about 20 tools (`docs/research/survey-2026-11.md`) checked what exists.
- **Decision:** Build nofluke: a thin, well-tested layer offering a file-driven batch ask/tell CLI, deterministic
  resume, an append-only history with provenance, and a noise protocol (evaluation seeds, re-evaluation of leaders,
  mean / n / lower-confidence-bound selection). Optimisation strategies are built-in baselines or wrapped from Optuna.
- **Alternatives:** Modernise GOE as a standalone GA engine - more code to own, and the evidence says a GA loses to
  TPE / Bayesian optimisation at this budget. Don't build anything, script Optuna or SMAC3 inside each client - every
  client would re-implement the CLI, determinism and noise handling, which no tool provides.
- **Consequences:** The name and repository changed (D4). A GA survives only as a possible later strategy for
  binary/subset spaces. Revisit if Optuna's CLI gains batch asks, deterministic resume and a noise protocol.
- **Evidence / source:** NeurIPS 2020 BBO challenge, 128 evaluations: TuRBO 88.9, Ax 87.0, TPE 82.4, Nevergrad
  (1+1) 80.0, pycma 78.7, random 75.8; authors: evolutionary methods "generally require thousands of evaluations"
  (Turner et al. 2021, arXiv 2104.10201) - established. Optuna 5.1 CLI `ask`/`tell`: experimental, one trial per
  call, flat space, seeded asks repeat identical params (run by the survey agent) - established. No surveyed tool
  offers the CLI + determinism + noise protocol combination - established for the tools surveyed.

## D2. nofluke knows nothing about its clients and never runs jobs (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The first client is a neuroscience project on a Slurm cluster with key-only ssh; others will differ.
- **Decision:** nofluke hands out candidates and receives scores through files or Python calls. It never submits
  jobs, holds credentials, opens ssh connections or imports client code, ML frameworks or simulators. Evaluator
  backends limited to a local Python function and a local subprocess command template; Slurm stays in the client
  (it can wrap `nofluke ask` / `tell` around `sbatch`, or use submitit itself).
- **Alternatives:** A built-in Slurm/submitit backend - couples nofluke to one scheduler and to cluster access.
- **Consequences:** Enforced by `[tool.docmap.forbid]` (torch, jax, tensorflow, neuron, submitit, pandas). The agent
  skill documents the client-side Slurm pattern.
- **Evidence / source:** simple_complex_v1 request §4, §7 (`docs/requests/simple_complex_v1.md`).

## D3. Core needs only numpy; Optuna is an optional, lazily imported backend (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** Clients run on clusters and lab machines where heavy dependencies hurt; Optuna brings TPE, GP and
  NSGA-II and a large user base but also sqlalchemy and alembic.
- **Decision:** `pip install nofluke` needs numpy only. Built-in strategies: random and Latin hypercube. YAML space
  files need the `yaml` extra; Optuna samplers need the `optuna` extra and are imported only inside
  `nofluke.strategies.optuna_backend`. nofluke does not use Optuna storage: the journal (D5) is the only state, and
  Optuna samplers run on an in-memory study rebuilt from it at each ask (D7).
- **Alternatives:** nofluke as an Optuna sampler / on Optuna storage - inherits Optuna's non-deterministic resume and
  flat CLI space. Optuna as a hard dependency - heavier install for clients that only need random/LHS.
- **Consequences:** Rebuilding an in-memory Optuna study per ask costs O(history), negligible at 200 evaluations.
- **Evidence / source:** survey (`docs/research/survey-2026-11.md`), Optuna storage and sampler RNG behaviour.

## D4. New name and repository: nofluke; GOE is frozen (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** After D1 "Genetic Optimization Engine" misdescribes the project.
- **Decision:** New repository `nofluke` (PyPI name free on 2026-11-17). The GOE repository got a README pointing
  here and is otherwise frozen. No GOE code is carried over; its ideas (mutation operators, choice parameters)
  inform a possible later evolutionary strategy.
- **Alternatives:** noisetune, quietune, truetune, slowtune, trialledger (owner chose nofluke).
- **Consequences:** GitHub repository `Horef/nofluke` still to be created (owner approval).
- **Evidence / source:** owner, 2026-11-17.

## D5. State is one append-only JSONL journal per study folder (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** State must survive crashes, live on network file systems shared with a cluster login node, be read
  by humans and other languages, and resume deterministically.
- **Decision:** A study is a folder holding `journal.jsonl`: one JSON event per line (study, ask, tell, ...; formats
  in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`), appended and fsynced under a lock file before any output is shown. The in-memory state is
  rebuilt by replaying the journal; nothing else is authoritative. Asked candidates are recorded with their params,
  so resuming never re-runs a strategy for a past ask.
- **Alternatives:** SQLite - locking is unreliable on NFS, not human-readable, harder from other languages. Pickled
  optimiser state (Nevergrad, pycma) - tied to library versions, opaque.
- **Consequences:** Replay is O(events); fine for thousands of evaluations. An incomplete last line (torn write) is
  moved to a side file before the next append, since it was never acknowledged.
- **Evidence / source:** Optuna's JournalFileBackend uses the same idea for NFS (survey, s1.a) - established.

## D7. Determinism: proposals are a pure function of (config, seed, history at ask time) (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** simple_complex_v1 needs "same seed and same tells give the same candidates"; Optuna does not persist
  sampler RNG state, so restarts repeat its random stream (survey).
- **Decision:** Every random draw uses a `numpy.random.Generator` derived with `SeedSequence(study_seed,
  spawn_key=(purpose, index))` from `nofluke.rng`, where index is the candidate or evaluation number. A strategy
  sees the history as completed evaluations sorted by evaluation id, plus pending candidates, so the order in which
  results arrive within one tell does not matter; which results were known at each ask does. Optuna samplers are
  seeded per candidate from the same derivation and run on a freshly rebuilt in-memory study.
- **Alternatives:** Persist a pickled RNG - fragile across versions and processes.
- **Consequences:** Tests replay identical operation sequences in fresh processes and compare candidates. A change
  that alters proposals for the same inputs is a breaking change (AGENTS.md conventions).
- **Evidence / source:** numpy SeedSequence spawn keys (numpy docs); survey finding on Optuna CLI determinism.

## D8. Noise protocol: a rolling, stateless re-evaluation policy (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** Noise SE ≈ the differences sought; at B = 128 only gaps of about 1σ can be resolved, and only for a
  few finalists (n ≈ 2(zσ/d)²). Results arrive out of order, so per-race state is fragile.
- **Decision:** Each ask fills its slots in this order: (1) retries of failed evaluations; (2) re-evaluations;
  (3) new candidates. A re-evaluation slot is used when the share of re-evaluations among issued evaluations would
  stay ≤ `reeval_share` (default 1/3), at least `min_candidates` (default 8) candidates have a result, and the
  plausible-best set S = {i : UCB_i ≥ max_j LCB_j} (posterior bounds, z = `z`, default 1.5) has a member below
  `max_replicates` (default 6) counting pending evaluations. The member with the fewest (completed + pending)
  evaluations is chosen, ties by highest shrunk mean then lowest candidate id. In the final `finalist_share` of
  the budget (default 8 %) every slot is a re-evaluation while S has a member below the cap. The policy is
  recomputed from the state at every ask. Clarified while implementing (2026-11-17): re-evaluation ties use the
  full D9 rank order (shrunk mean, then mean − zσ_i/√n_i, then id), so equal shrunk means early on fall to the
  better raw mean; a finalist slot with no eligible member of S becomes a new candidate; retries do not count as
  issued evaluations in the share.
- **Alternatives:** F-race / Hoeffding races - eat the budget or never eliminate at this n. SMAC intensification -
  sequential and stateful. OCBA - poor at tiny budgets. Successive halving - blocks on out-of-order results.
- **Consequences:** About 2/3 of the budget explores. Defaults are plausible, not tuned: the benchmark harness must
  test them against "no re-evaluation" (D11). `reeval_share: 0` turns the protocol off.
- **Evidence / source:** `docs/research/design-research-2026-11.md` §1 (LUCB/OCBA-flavoured; plausible).

## D9. "Best" is the empirical-Bayes shrunk mean, reported with n and a lower bound (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The max of K noisy single evaluations is optimistically biased by about σ·E[max of K normals]
  (≈ 2.65σ at K = 128); overtuning is severe in ~10 % of HPO runs (Schneider, Bischl & Feurer 2025).
- **Decision:** Per candidate i with n_i completed values (in "higher is better" units): mean ȳ_i; noise variance
  σ_i² = (ν0·s_p² + (n_i−1)·s_i²)/(ν0 + n_i − 1) with ν0 = `nu0` (default 4) and s_p² the pooled within-candidate
  variance when at least 3 candidates have n ≥ 2, else `prior_sd`², else the variance of ȳ across candidates
  (conservative: all spread treated as noise). Prior mean m = mean of ȳ; τ² = max(0, Var(ȳ) − mean(σ_i²/n_i));
  shrinkage B_i = τ²/(τ² + σ_i²/n_i); shrunk mean μ̂_i = m + B_i(ȳ_i − m); posterior SE_i = √(B_i·σ_i²/n_i);
  LCB/UCB = μ̂_i ∓ z·SE_i. Candidates are ranked by μ̂, ties by ȳ_i − z·σ_i/√n_i, then id. `best` reports ȳ, n, μ̂,
  SE, LCB and the number of candidates the pick was made over.
- **Alternatives:** Best single observation - the fluke the project is named against. Raw-mean LCB - over-penalises
  n = 1 without using the population. GP posterior mean - needs a model; the Optuna GP backend may add it later.
- **Consequences:** When τ² = 0 all shrunk means equal m and the tie-break decides; `best` says so. A test-set check
  of the top 1-3 picks stays the client's job (documented in the README and the agent skill).
- **Evidence / source:** research §2 (direction established, exact shrinkage plausible).

## D10. Evaluation seeds: replicate r gets the same seed for every candidate (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** The evaluator needs an explicit seed; shared seeds (common random numbers) make comparisons paired,
  fresh seeds protect against seed-specific luck. No source tests CRN for neural-network training.
- **Decision:** Every evaluation carries `seed` = an integer in [0, 2³¹) derived from (study seed, "eval-seed", r)
  for replicate r of the candidate (`seed_mode: shared`, default), or from (study seed, "eval-seed", candidate, r)
  (`seed_mode: per_candidate`). A retry keeps the replicate's seed. The selection statistics (D9) treat
  replicates as independent; paired analysis is deferred until data show positive correlation.
- **Alternatives:** Engine-chosen fresh random seeds - not paired, harder to audit.
- **Consequences:** Replicate 0 of every candidate uses the same seed: the first pass is a fair comparison.
- **Evidence / source:** research §3 (plausible; CRN benefit for NN training unresolved).

## D11. Strategies: Latin-hypercube start, then random (built-in) or Optuna TPE/GP (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** At 100-200 evaluations in mixed spaces SMAC, TPE and CMA-ES lead recent benchmarks, but random
  search is a tough baseline and rankings settle late (carps, Benjamins et al. 2025).
- **Decision:** Every strategy's first `n_init` new candidates (default `clip(budget // 8, 8, 20)`) come from one
  Latin-hypercube design over the whole space. After that: `random` (default, numpy only), `tpe` (Optuna TPE,
  multivariate, constant liar), `gp` (Optuna GPSampler, opt-in for continuous spaces). A strategy proposes one
  candidate at a time from (space, history, rng for that candidate index); pending candidates are part of the
  history so batch proposals do not collide. Missing optional packages fail loudly at `init`, never fall back.
- **Alternatives:** An "auto" strategy that depends on what is installed - breaks determinism across machines.
- **Consequences:** Benchmarks compare every strategy with random and LHS at equal budget and identical noise
  policy, plus "noise protocol off".
- **Evidence / source:** research §4-§5 (plausible).

## D6. Answers to simple_complex_v1's wish list (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** `docs/requests/simple_complex_v1.md` (read-only) lists must-haves and options for the first client.
- **Decision:** Accepted as asked: ask/tell with partial batches, out-of-order results, failures with one retry
  (D8, CONTRACTS §3); serialisable space with log floats/ints, choice, bool and conditionals (CONTRACTS §1); journal
  persistence and deterministic resume (D5, D7); elitism replaced by re-evaluation of the plausible-best set and
  shrunk-mean selection (D8, D9); evaluation seed in every candidate (D10); machine-readable history with provenance
  (`export`, CONTRACTS §3-4); pyproject, numpy-only core, pytest, CI, CHANGELOG; the CLI exactly as sketched plus
  `pending`, `abandon`, `done`, `verify`; evaluator backends local function and subprocess template (D2).
  Changed: no GA operators or mutation-scale adaptation (D1, D11; strategies are LHS + random/TPE/GP); no Slurm
  backend in nofluke (D2: the client wraps sbatch; submitit stays client-side); Optuna as an optional backend
  rather than nofluke as an Optuna sampler (D3). Deferred: multi-fidelity and population-based training (noise ≈
  effect makes early cuts risky, research §8; PBT needs in-process checkpoints), multi-objective, steady-state
  beyond `optimize`, the agent skill (after the CLI is tested).
- **Alternatives:** Implementing the list literally (GA core, Slurm backend) - see D1, D2.
- **Consequences:** simple_complex_v1 can start once the MVP plan (`docs/plans/mvp.md`) is done.
- **Evidence / source:** this log's D1-D11; the request file.

## D12. Public GitHub repository; the agent skill lives in this repository (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** BRIEF open questions on visibility and on where the "set up a nofluke search" agent skill lives.
- **Decision:** `Horef/nofluke` is public (MIT). The agent skill is versioned with the library in `skills/`.
- **Alternatives:** Private repository; the skill in the claude-plugins marketplace repository.
- **Consequences:** The skill changes in the same commits as the CLI it documents; a marketplace entry can point here.
- **Evidence / source:** owner, 2026-11-17.

## D13. Optuna backend details (2026-11-17; status: accepted)
- **Context:** D3 and D11 fixed the shape of the Optuna backend; implementing it raised smaller choices.
- **Decision:** Samplers get `n_startup_trials = 4` (the LHS start already explores; below 4 results the sampler
  draws seeded random points). TPE: `multivariate`, `constant_liar`, and `group` only when the space has `when`
  conditions. Pending candidates are replayed as RUNNING trials (verified to move TPE and GP proposals); failed
  candidates are not replayed (Optuna 5.1's TPE and GP ignore FAIL trials). Choices and booleans are passed as
  category indices matched by type and value, so 1, 1.0 and True stay distinct. `strategy.options` are extra sampler
  keyword arguments; `seed` and unknown options are refused at `init`. `gp` needs torch and scipy (extra `gp`).
- **Alternatives:** Optuna defaults (`n_startup_trials = 10`) - repeats the LHS exploration; replaying FAIL trials
  - no effect on the current samplers.
- **Consequences:** GP models only unconditional parameters (conditional ones are sampled at random): use `tpe`
  for conditional spaces. TPE proposals are numpy-only and reproducible across machines on one Optuna version; GP
  proposals depend on torch/scipy floating point and are reproducible per environment only. Any Optuna upgrade may
  change proposals for the same inputs; the journal's provenance records the version and `verify` detects drift.
  Tested only on Optuna 5.1.0. ask(1) at 200 completed candidates: TPE ≈ 0.01 s, GP ≈ 0.1-0.15 s.
- **Evidence / source:** backend implementation and probes, 2026-11-17 (`tests/test_optuna_backend.py`).
